Rashi on Sanhedrin 19a:12:1.hebrew: ובנה אחריה - בנה הקטן לא יהלך אחריה, אלא לפניה:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 19a:12:1.english: And her son behind her - Her young son should not walk behind her, but rather in front of her.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 19a:12:2.hebrew: משום מעשה שהיה - שגנבוהו פריצים מאחריה ונתנוהו בבית, וכשחזרה ולא ראתהו, התחילה צועקת ובוכה. בא אחד מהם ואמר: "בואי ואראנו ליך", ונכנסה אחריו, ועינו אותה:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 19a:12:2.english: Because of an incident that happened - For bandits abducted him from behind her and put him in a house. And when she turned around and did not see him, she began crying out and weeping. One of them came and said: “Come, and I will show him to you.” And she entered after him, and they violated her.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 19a:12:4.hebrew: משום ייחוד - שמא ילך אדם שם, ואם לא ישמע קול אדם — יכנס ויתייחד שם. ותנן (קידושין דף פ:): לא יתייחד אדם עם ב' נשים. ובבית הכסא שבשדות קמיירי, שהיה בית הכסא שלהם בשדה חוץ לעיר, והכל ניפנים שם:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 19a:12:4.english: Because of seclusion - Lest a man go there, and if he does not hear a person’s voice, he will enter and be secluded there. And we learned in a Mishnah (Kiddushin 80b): “A man may not be secluded with two women.” And [the Gemara] is dealing with a bathroom in the fields, for their bathroom was in a field outside the city, and everyone would relieve themselves there.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 19a:13:1.hebrew: בין שאבלים עומדין שם כו' - וכך הורה לי, שאין שינוי מנהג בדבר: בין שהיו אבלים עומדין, בין אבלים עוברין — אין כאן קלקול:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 19a:13:1.english: Whether the mourners stand there, etc. - And thus he instructed me: that a difference in custom makes no difference in this matter; whether the mourners were standing or the mourners were passing by, there is no flaw here.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 19a:14:1.english: And he says: May you be consoled - It is a baraita.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 19a:14:2.hebrew: נחשא קא רמי - סימן הוא מטיל להם להרע, שיצטרכו לנחומים?! בתמיה:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 19a:14:2.english: He is casting an omen - Is he casting upon them an omen for misfortune, that they should need consolation?! [This is said] in astonishment.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 19a:16:1.hebrew: תנו עיניכם - לדונו בדין, ולא תחניפו, ולא תשאו פניו:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 19a:16:1.english: Set your eyes - To judge him according to the law, and do not flatter [him], and do not show him favoritism.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 19a:17:1.hebrew: ויעידו בך - שעבדך הרג את הנפש, דעבדו כחמורו, והפסד ממון הוא לו. לפיכך, צריך לדונו בפניו:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 19a:17:1.english: And they will testify against you - [Namely,] that your slave killed a person. For one’s slave is like his donkey, and it is a monetary loss to him; therefore, it is necessary to judge [the slave] in his presence.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 19a:1:1.english: And a positive mitzva does not [override] - [Namely, the mitzva:] “Her husband’s brother shall go in unto her” (Deuteronomy 25:5).

Rashi on Sanhedrin 19a:2:1.hebrew: ביאה ראשונה - דייבום מקיימא מצות עשה, ביאה שניה — לאו מצות יבום הוא:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 19a:2:1.english: The first act of intercourse - of levirate marriage fulfills a positive commandment, [whereas] a second act of intercourse is not the commandment of levirate marriage.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 19a:4:1.hebrew: ומן המקדש לא יצא - בכהן גדול אונן כתיב (ויקרא כא), דהא כתיב לעיל מיניה: "לאביו ולאמו לא יטמא":
Rashi on Sanhedrin 19a:4:1.english: “And from the Sanctuary he shall not emerge” - It is written concerning a High Priest [who is an] onen [a mourner prior to burial] (Leviticus 21), for it is written prior to it: “He shall not defile himself for his father or for his mother.”

Rashi on Sanhedrin 19a:6:1.hebrew: מקדושתו לא יצא - כלומר, יעשה חיזוק לדבריו, שלא יגרום לצאת מקדושה וליטמא:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 19a:6:1.english: From his sanctity he shall not emerge - That is to say, he must make a safeguard for [the Torah's] words, so that he does not cause [himself] to depart from sanctity and become defiled.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 19a:7:1.english: His bitterness - The bitterness of his heart.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 19a:8:1.hebrew: משוח שעבר - כגון שאירע בו פסול בכהן גדול ומינו אחר תחתיו, וכשעבר פסולו של ראשון — חוזר לעבודתו, ושני — קרא ליה "משוח שעבר":
Rashi on Sanhedrin 19a:8:1.english: A former anointed [High Priest] - For example, where a disqualification occurred to the High Priest and they appointed another in his place; and when the disqualification of the first passed, he returns to his service, and the second [one] — [the Baraita] calls him "a former anointed [priest]".

Rashi on Sanhedrin 19a:9:1.english: His mind will become distraught - [The mind] of the High Priest.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 19a:9:2.english: He is happy about me - He rejoices in my mourning.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 19a:9:3.hebrew: ש"מ - מדקתני: סגן מיכן והעם מיכן וכהן באמצע — היינו סגן היינו ממונה דמתני', דקתני: הממונה ממצעו לכהן, ונותנו בינו לבין העם:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 19a:9:3.english: Learn from it - Since it teaches: The deputy is on this side, and the people are on that side, and the priest is in the middle — the deputy is [the same as] the appointed one of the Mishnah, as it teaches: The appointed one places the priest in the middle, and sets him between himself and the people.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 19a:9:4.hebrew: וש"מ - כן מנהג תנחומין שורה: שיהו אבלים עומדין במקומן, וכל העם עוברין — איש איש כשמגיע אצל האבל מנחמו ועובר; מדקתני: "כשהוא עובר לנחם", וגבי מתנחם קתני: "כשהוא עומד בשורה להתנחם":
Rashi on Sanhedrin 19a:9:4.english: And learn from it - Such is the custom of consolation [in] a line: that the mourners stand in their place and all the people pass by — each person, when he reaches the mourner, consoles him and passes by; since it teaches: “When he passes by to console,” and regarding [one who is] being consoled, it teaches: “When he stands in the line to be consoled.”

Rashi on Sanhedrin 19a:9:5.hebrew: אבלים לשמאל המנחמים - מדקתני: "ואבל וכל העם משמאלו", והרי הוא היה מן המנחמין, וקתני אבלים לשמאלו:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 19a:9:5.english: Mourners [stand] to the left of the consolers - Since it teaches: "And [the] mourner and all the people [are] on his left," and behold, he was among the consolers, and [thus] it teaches [that the] mourners [stand] to his left.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 19a:15:1.hebrew: אבל מלכי בית דוד דן ודנין אותו - וא"ת: וכי איך יכול לדון? והא אמרינן לעיל: "אין מושיבין מלך בסנהדרין", משום דכתיב: "לא תענה על ריב"! וי"ל: דהכא מיירי דוקא לדון דיני ממונות, דלא איכפת לן אם לא יוכלו לענות אחריו, כדאמרי' (לקמן סנהדרין לב:): דיני ממונות מתחילין מן הגדול. ומיהו קשה, דאפילו דיני נפשות נמי אשכחן, כדכתיב (שמואל א כ״ה:ל״ה): "ויחגור [גם] דוד [את] חרבו", דהא לקמן (סנהדרין דף לו:) ילפינן מיניה דדיני נפשות מתחילין מן הצד; וכיון שהיה חושב דוד עצמו למלך, היאך היה דן עמהם? וי"ל: כיון שהיה אותו הדין לכבודו, על שמרד נבל בו, לא היה לו בושת אם ידברו האחרים לפניו. אבל בשאר מלכי בית דוד, ודאי אין דנין דיני נפשות, כדפרישית:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 19a:15:1.english: “But [with regard to] the kings of the house of David, he judges and they judge him” - And if you say: But how can he judge? Behold, didn't we say above [18a]: “One does not seat a king on the Sanhedrin,” because it is written: “You shall not speak in a dispute [al riv]” [interpreted as: do not dispute the greatest judge]! And one can say: Here it is dealing specifically with judging monetary cases, where we do not care if they cannot dispute after him, as we say below (Sanhedrin 32b): Monetary cases begin from the greatest [judge]. However, this is difficult, for even [regarding] capital cases, we also find [that David judged], as it is written (I Samuel 25:35 [25:13]): “David [also] girded [on his] sword,” for below (Sanhedrin 36b) we derive from this that capital cases begin from the side; and since David considered himself a king, how could he judge with them? And one can say: Since that trial was for his honor, because Nabal had rebelled against him, he felt no humiliation if the others spoke before him. But with the other kings of the house of David, they certainly do not judge capital cases, as I explained.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 19a:17:1.hebrew: ינאי המלך עמוד על רגליך ויעידו בך - ואם תאמר: והא אמרינן התם, אפי' ת"ח א"צ לעמוד, משום דהאי עשה והאי עשה, ועשה דכבוד תורה עדיף, כדאמר בפרק שבועת העדות (שבועות דף ל: ושם)? וכיון דחכם אינו צריך לעמוד, כ"ש מלך — דטפי עדיף מלך מת"ח, כדקאמר לקמן: דאפי' למ"ד הרב שמחל על כבודו כבודו מחול, מלך שמחל על כבודו אין כבודו מחול, שנאמר: "שום תשים עליך מלך" וכו'! וי"ל: דודאי עשה דכבוד תורה עדיף, וא"כ אעפ"י שאין ת"ח היה צריך לעמוד, ינאי היה צריך לעמוד. והאי דת"ח יכול למחול על כבודו משא"כ מלך — הוא משום קרא דקאמר: "שום" וגו', שתהא אימתו עליך, כי כבודו בא לו משום דמצות המקום כך הוא, ואין יכול להפקיע מצות המקום; אבל ת"ח, תורתו דיליה, ויכול למחול היטב על כבודו, דשלו היא, כדאמרי' במס' ע"ז (דף יט.): בתחלה נקראת על שמו של הקב"ה, ולבסוף נקראת על שמו, שנאמר: אם בתורת ה' חפצו ובתורתו יהגה יומם ולילה:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 19a:17:1.english: “Yannai the king, stand on your feet and let them testify against you” - And if you should say: But don’t we say there [in Shevuot 30b] that even a Torah scholar is not required to stand, because this is a positive commandment [“and both people shall stand”] and that is a positive commandment [“and you shall honor the face of an elder”], and the positive commandment of honoring the Torah takes precedence, as [the Gemara] says in the chapter [entitled] Shevuat HaEdut (Shevuot 30b and there)? And since a sage is not required to stand, all the more so a king — for a king is of even greater standing than a Torah scholar, as [the Gemara] says later (19b) that even according to the one who says [that regarding] a teacher who waives his honor, his honor is waived, [regarding] a king who waives his honor, his honor is not waived, as it is stated: “You shall surely set a king over you” (Deuteronomy 17:15), etc.! And one can say: Indeed, the positive commandment of honoring the Torah takes precedence, and if so, even though a Torah scholar would not have needed to stand, Yannai was required to stand. And this [distinction], that a Torah scholar can waive his honor whereas a king cannot, is because of the verse which states: “You shall surely set...” — that his awe shall be upon you; for his honor comes to him because such is the commandment of the Omnipresent, and he cannot abrogate the commandment of the Omnipresent. But [as for] a Torah scholar, his Torah is his own, and he can certainly waive his honor, as it belongs to him, as we say in Tractate Avodah Zarah (19a): At first it is called by the name of the Holy One, Blessed be He, and ultimately it is called by his own name, as it is stated: “[whose delight is in the law of the Lord,] and in his Torah he meditates day and night” (Psalms 1:2).

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 19a:17:2.hebrew: ינאי המלך עמוד על רגליך וכו' - והא דאמרינן פרק שבועת העדות (שבועות דף ל. ושם) שאם רצו להושיב שניהם מושיבין, דאינו אסור אלא אחד עומד ואחד יושב — ואם כן, לא היה המלך צריך לעמוד, ובלבד שישב אותו שכנגדו? וי"ל: דדיני נפשות שאני. אי נמי: הכא הוי קבלת עדות, וקבלת עדות כשעת גמר דין; ובשעת גמר דין אמרינן פרק שבועת העדות (שבועות דף ל: ושם): דברי הכל דיינים בישיבה ובעלי דינין בעמידה. ואם כן, יש ליזהר כשב"ד מושיבין שני בעלי דינין שלא ישבו בשעת קבלת העדות ולא בשעת גמר דין, דשעת קבלת העדות כמו גמר דין חשוב:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 19a:17:2.english: "Yannai the king, stand on your feet," etc. - And [as for] that which we say in the chapter [entitled] Shevuot HaEdut (Shevuot 30a and there), that if they wished to seat both of them, they seat [them], as it is forbidden only [for] one [to be] standing and one sitting — and if so, the king should not have needed to stand, provided that the one opposing him would sit? And one can say: Capital cases are different. Alternatively: Here, it was the acceptance of testimony, and the acceptance of testimony is like the time of the verdict. And at the time of the verdict, we say in the chapter [entitled] Shevuot HaEdut (Shevuot 30b and there): Everyone agrees [that] the judges are sitting and the litigants are standing. And if so, one must be careful, when the court seats both litigants, that they should not sit at the time of the acceptance of the testimony nor at the time of the verdict, as the time of the acceptance of testimony is considered like the verdict.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 19a:9:1.hebrew: היינו סגן היינו ממונה - וליכא למימר דהיינו משוח שעבר, דפשיטא דלא מיקרי ממונה. והר"ר יעקב בר' יהוצדק פירש, דמשמע ממתני' גם כשהוא מתנחם מאחרים דממונה ממצעו, ומוסיף הוא: "כל העם אומר לו וכו'", ובבריי' וקאמר: משוח שעבר לא אתי גביה:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 19a:9:1.english: "The deputy is the appointed person" - And one cannot say that the appointed person is the previously anointed High Priest, for it is obvious that a former High Priest is not called "appointed." And Rabbi Yaakov, son of Rabbi Yehotzadak, explained that it is implied from the Mishnah that even when he is consoled by others, the appointed official places him in the middle, and the Mishnah merely adds: "All the people say to him, etc."; and in the baraita it says: The previously anointed High Priest does not come near him.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 19a:9:2.hebrew: ושמע מינה אבלים משמאל וכו' - פירוש: דתנן "ממצעו בינו לבין העם", בברייתא קתני "ראש בית האב ואבלים משמאלו וכל העם" — אלמא שיהו העם ראשונים משמאלו, ואם כן האבלים היו משמאל העם:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 19a:9:2.english: "And learn from it that the mourners [stand] to the left, etc." - Explanation: For we learned in the Mishnah: "[The appointed person] places him in the middle, between himself and the people," and in the baraita it is taught: "The head of the patrilineal family, and the mourners, and all the people [are] to his left." This indicates that the people were first to his left, and if so, the mourners were to the left of the people.
